title: Capacity synchronization and cost attenuation roadmap 2026
author: Riley Thompson
content:
Summary:
This roadmap defines a coordinated, platform-level program to synchronize capacity allocation across the serving runtime and orchestrator, reduce per-token cost through adaptive policies, and provide deterministic operational guarantees for tenants during demand spikes. The program is intentionally cross-cutting: it touches batching, cache coherence, tenant priority scoring, predictive allocation, and observability.

Scope:
- Systems: batching-router, predictive-allocator, prefix-cache, eviction-controller, tenant-priority-scorer, cost-fanout, observability-signal-proxy.
- Workstreams: real-time capacity sync, demand forecasting, soft quota economics, cost-aware routing, SLO-preserving degradation.
- Excludes: hardware procurement and long-term regional capacity expansion (handled by SRE capacity planning).

Goals & success metrics (measurable):
1) Reduce hosted per-1M-token compute cost by 18% (baseline: avg $X.XX per 1M tokens measured across Jan–Mar 2026).
2) Keep P95 token latency degradation under 30% during 2x normal traffic bursts for tiered tenants.
3) Reduce manual intervention rate for tenant eviction incidents by 60% within 6 months.
4) Provide a single capacity-canonical view (API) with <5s staleness for scheduler decisions.

Current state summary (concise):
- Batching decisions live in batching-router; predictive-allocator produces daily allocation hints; no shared runtime cache of near-term demand forecasts.
- Prefix-cache coherence is eventual; eviction-controller runs per-pool heuristics leading to noisy tenant eviction events.
- Cost signals are emitted but not acted on by fast path routing; cost-fanout exists as an offline job.

Principles guiding design:
- SLO-first: all cost savings must preserve declared SLAs for paying tenants.
- Visibility: every allocation decision must be explainable via observability traces and tokenized cost attribution.
- Graceful degradation: prefer soft-rate-limits, queueing, and lightweight fallback models over hard evictions.
- Incremental rollout: staged feature flags, canaries, operator override.

Major initiatives & milestones (quartered):
- Q1 2026: Foundations
  - Implement capacity-canonical API (GET /v1/internal/capacity?region=...) with 5s TTL, wire to predictive-allocator.
  - Emit tenant short-term forecast (t+0..t+60m) from predictive-allocator; schema: forecast_time, tenant_id, expected_tps, confidence.
  - Instrument cost-fanout to tag routing traces with predictiveness score.
- Q2 2026: Fast-path cost-aware routing and cache coherency
  - Add cost-aware routing plugin to batching-router (configurable weight: cost_vs_latency).
  - Implement prefix-cache lease protocol to reduce cross-pool thrash (lease duration default 120s).
  - Create dashboard templates for capacity sync health (see observability section).
- Q3 2026: Controlled degradation & tenant economics
  - Launch soft-quota slab enforcement with backpressure hooks to tenant SDKs and 429-with-retry-after semantics.
  - Introduce per-tenant burst credits and auto-buydown simulation in staging.
  - Run 3 platform gamedays exercising 2x–5x burst scenarios.
- Q4 2026: Operator surfaces & cost automation
  - Operator UI: capacity conflict resolver and tenant cost-recommendations (open to Platform Ops).
  - Automated model: from simulations, begin auto-adjusting batch-size ceilings during sustained high-cost windows.

Technical approach (detailed):
1) Capacity-canonical API
   - Purpose: single source of truth for capacity units (GPU-pool tokens, warm instances, op slots).
   - Contract: 5s staleness max, JSON schema versioned, fields: pool_id, available_slots, predicted_free_slots_60m, observed_util_p95.
   - Implementation notes: use leaderless gossip sync with CRDT counter for available_slots to avoid central throttles.

2) Short-term forecasting (predictive-allocator)
   - Inputs: rolling telemetry (per-tenant TPS, prefix cache hits, queued requests), rate-of-change features, calendar features, tenant plan tier.
   - Output: per-tenant, per-pool forecast for 60m horizon with confidence band.
   - Model lifecycle: start with light-weight SARIMA/exp-smoothing baseline; A/B candidate neural model in Q2 for comparison.

3) Cost-aware routing plugin (batching-router)
   - Config knobs: cost_weight (0..1), latency_weight (0..1), min_priority_floor.
   - Behavior: for requests evaluated on fast-path, compute routing score = cost_weight * est_cost + latency_weight * est_latency; prefer routes with lower score.

4) Prefix-cache lease protocol
   - Lease table entries: prefix, owner_pool, lease_expires_at, lease_epoch.
   - Safety: two-phase renew with jitter; eviction-controller respects lease before hard eviction.

SLO and impact table (ascii):
+-------------------------------+----------------------+-----------------+
| Metric                        | Baseline (Jan 2026)  | Target (Q4 2026) | Notes           |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+-----------------+
| Host P95 token latency        | 620ms                | <= 750ms under 2x burst | preserve customer-grade latency |
| Eviction incident count/month | 25                   | <=10            | manual interventions reduced |
| Per-1M token compute cost     | $X.XX                | -18%            | measured host-wide |
| Capacity-canonical staleness  | N/A                  | <=5s            | required for scheduler correctness |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+-----------------+

Cost modeling assumptions (short):
- Average sequence length: 70 tokens; average batch pop size 8 in baseline.
- GPU hour normalized cost: $Y/hr; quantization and kernel selection improvements excluded here.
- Conservative benefit estimate assumes 10% batch size uplift and 12% cache-hit improvement from prefix lease.

Observability & dashboards:
- New dashboards (templates in Grafana):
  - Capacity sync overview: capacity-canonical freshness, pool utilization heatmap, forecast accuracy (MAE, MAPE).
  - Cost vs latency tradeoff: cost_weight sweep, per-tenant p50/p95 latencies, and cost-per-token.
  - Eviction incident triage dashboard: event timeline, lease reassignments, operator actions.
- Traces: ensure routing decisions attach tags (predictive_score, capacity_epoch, decision_reason).
- Alerts:
  - Severity P1: capacity-canonical api >10s error rate >2% for 5m -> page oncall SRE.
  - Severity P2: forecast MAE > 40% on any pool for 30m -> notify platform-operators channel.

Rollout plan & safe guards:
1) Local dev and unit tests for lease protocol + backward compatibility tests for batching-router.
2) Staging canary: enable capacity-canonical reads in staging; run dry-run of cost-aware routing without action.
3) Shadow pilot: in a small US pool (pool-id: us-east-dev-04), enable routing decisions but only observe impact for 72h.
4) Limited production canary (1%) for Q2 features with abort-on-excess-error hooks.
5) Full rollout with operator ramp and runbook in place.

Sample operator commands & config examples:
- Capacity-canonical health check (kubectl):
  kubectl exec -n platform svc/capacity-canonical -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/health | jq

- Example forecast schema (YAML):
  - tenant_id: "tenant-123"
  - forecast_time: "2026-02-07T14:00:00Z"
  - expected_tps: "42.7"
  - confidence: "0.92"
Risk analysis & mitigations:
- Risk: Forecast model underfits high-variance tenants -> mitigation: conservative safety margins + operator override; run gamedays.
- Risk: Lease protocol adds latency to cache accesses -> mitigation: keep lease local for reads; renew asynchronously.
- Risk: Cost-weighted routing causes latency regressions for latency-sensitive customers -> mitigation: min_priority_floor, opt-out per-tenant.

Ownership, stakeholders & contact list (primary):
- Program lead: Riley Thompson (Platform Engineering)
- Predictive model owner: Aisha Rahman (Applied ML and Evals)
- Runtime changes (batching-router): Marco Alvarez (Serving Runtime)
- Observability & dashboards: Priya Singh (Eng Platform Observability)
- Platform Ops: Jenna Ortiz (Platform Ops)

Dependencies & cross-team items:
- eng-serving-runtime: kernel scheduling knobs to support dynamic batch ceilings.
- eng-infra: platform RBAC changes for operator UI.
- eng-sre: capacity planning alignment for predicted free slots.

Open questions (to resolve in Q1 planning):
1) What is the canonical token for capacity units (slots vs GPU-shares)? Proposed: start with slot unit and map to GPU-shares in translation layer.
2) Acceptable default lease length for prefix-cache across regions? Proposed default: 120s; evaluate at scale.
3) How aggressive should auto-buydown be for burst credits? Target: simulation in Q3.

Action items (next 30 days):
1) RFC: capacity-canonical API schema and auth (owner: Riley) — due 2026-01-05.
2) Prototype: short-term forecast emitter (owner: Aisha) — initial prototype by 2026-01-20.
3) Dashboard proto: capacity sync health dashboard (owner: Priya) — first draft 2026-01-25.
4) Runbook draft for eviction-controller respecting leases (owner: Marco) — 2026-02-10.
